findings.reason: the section-scoping owner is `is_section_scoped`/`unresolved_dependencies` in reckon/lifecycle.py, and the design should extend it to the gate path (as `unresolved_dependencies` already does for dependencies) or state why a gate's `gated_sections` is intentionally advisory-only, rather than shipping a second blocking projection that diverges from the one beside it.
findings.text: `unpassed_gate_blockers` projects every gate whose verdict is not `passed` into a whole-plan blocker row without consulting the gate's `gated_sections`, while the sibling derivation in the same file (`unresolved_dependencies`, reckon/lifecycle.py:26, via `is_section_scoped`) deliberately leaves section-scoped waits to the section that declares them; the plan's own gate carries `gated_sections` and roadmap honours it in `_gate_section_edges` (reckon/roadmap.py:268), so the same field is scoped in one consumer and ignored in the other, and the plan's own comment of 2026-09-24 records the consequence: a section-scoped gate makes `roadmap` report the whole plan `effective_status: blocked` with an empty `ready_now` though its other sections are ungated — the precise premature whole-plan blocking the plan exists to remove

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the derived half is one deep function pair: `unpassed_gate_blockers` projects gates into blocker rows and `effective_status` projects them over workflow status, behind a two-argument interface that three independent consumers share (serve._derive_lifecycle, mcp_views._blocking, roadmap). The parse/render/store/validate spread mirrors the pre-existing decisions/followups pattern rather than adding a new shape.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds `gated_sections` to the gate and roadmap scopes gate edges by it, but the blocker projection the plan routes gates through ignores it, forking the section-scoping rule that already owns this decision in the same file.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the section adds no CLI option and no MCP view (staleness rides the existing plan-read payload, the gate column is SPA presentation), and it names its retirements in its own text — `blocked` removed from the persistable status set, sprint activation ceased to be an operation at all, 45 persisted sprint-item statuses dropped, and the prose-gate tables retired through `retire_prose`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the existing machinery it extends and the code confirms each: `unpassed_gate_blockers`/`effective_status` (reckon/lifecycle.py:52,72), the decisions/followups semantic-element pattern for the gate element, `doccheck.lifecycle_staleness`/`authorisation_staleness` thresholds (reckon/doccheck.py:259,286) for staleness, and `focus_sprint_id` (reckon/project_state.py:1277) for derived sprint focus; the gate-representation decision records that followups-with-a-discriminator was considered and declined.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `unpassed_gate_blockers` (reckon/lifecycle.py:52) is a pure projection that reuses the existing `effective_status` derivation, and the plan states why the dependency derivation could not simply be extended for it: a gate is a declared blocker but not a dependency ref, so it needs its own row shape while still feeding the one blocking list.
